cards.text: Haggai, a prophet of the LORD, has already received messages from Him (Hag 1:1; 2:1; 2:10). Now the word of the LORD comes to Haggai again. Friend, back in the junk drawer, the only messages I ever got were takeout menus.

cards.question: This new word of the LORD comes to Haggai on that very same day, the twenty-fourth day of the month.

cards.text: This one's for Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and Haggai's the delivery guy. Friend, this package is HEAVY.

cards.question: In His message for Zerubbabel, what does the LORD say He's about to shake?

cards.text: Then the LORD gets specific about the nations, starting at the very top with their royal thrones. The only throne I've ever had is this gold base, and it doesn't even come with armrests.

cards.question: In His message for Zerubbabel, the LORD says He will protect the royal thrones of the nations.
The LORD says He'll overturn royal thrones. What else does He say He'll destroy among the nations?

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to the battlefield: He'll overturn chariots and their riders. Flipped like cookies off a spatula, and THOSE never land pretty.

cards.question: With the chariots overturned, how does the LORD say the horses and their riders will fall?

answers.text: Each by the sword of his brother
Each by a stone from a sling
Each under the waves of the sea

cards.text: Thrones flipping, chariots flipping, and then the LORD calls one man by name, his father's name too. "On that day," He says, He will take Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel.

cards.question: Zerubbabel is governor of Judah, but the LORD gives him another title. He calls Zerubbabel His ___.
On that day, what does the LORD say He will make His servant Zerubbabel like?
The LORD tells Zerubbabel why He'll make him like His signet ring. It's because the LORD has ___ him.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of Haggai's messages. It opens with 'For the second time that day,' right after the message of 2:10-19. The opening card never tells the baker about that earlier message that same day, or what is going on in Judah. It only says Haggai has received messages before and then spends its third sentence on a joke. The baker has no setup for the day or the situation.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The question says 'on that very same day, the twenty-fourth day of the month,' but no card has mentioned any day. The earlier date comes from Hag 2:10, and card 1 never gives it. 'That very same day' points back to something the baker never saw, so the baker can only guess.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 9 asks the baker to supply the exact phrase 'Each by the sword of his brother.' Card 8 gives nothing to reason from. This is guessing the wording of a prophetic line, not asking about its movement or meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks which word the LORD uses for Zerubbabel (servant, prophet or priest). No card gives the baker anything to reason from. It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The signet ring is the key image of the passage. It is asked with no story card setting it up, so signet ring, shepherd's staff and mighty sword can only be told apart by luck. This matches the Psalm 23 bad example of guessing a detail.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Most choice cards are discovery questions with no reasoning possible. Card 2 has no day given. Card 4 picks out what is shaken. Card 7 picks out what else is destroyed. Cards 9, 11 and 12 ask for exact wording or details. Only cards 6 and 13 are clear informed guesses. The story cards are too thin to support reasoned picks.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
